Subject: Draft MAP & evaluation timeline — proposal for pilot -> annual commit

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Per our conversation, I attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (Cloudwave_MAP_v1.2.pdf) that lays out:
- 6-week evaluation (engineering proofs + latency/cost benchmarks)
- KPIs for acceptance (99th p90 latency, tokens/unit cost target)
- Rollout milestones to move from pilot -> production ramp

A couple of commercial notes up-front: we typically structure a pilot with a small committed baseline and a ramp ladder that triggers incremental discounts as Cloudwave hits throughput milestones. I sketched a ladder in the attached term sheet (Commercial_Term_Sheet_CW-4921.xlsx) — happy to revise based on procurement constraints.

Next steps proposed:
1) Agree MAP milestones and measurement plan — by Nov 24
2) Provision pilot capacity and share test prompts — by Nov 30
3) Commercial term alignment and signature for pilot commit (DocuSign link to follow) — target Dec 3

If that cadence looks reasonable to you, I’ll loop in Marissa from CS to document success criteria and Karthik to finalize the pricing ladder.

Cheers,
Jordan

Jordan —

Appreciate the MAP draft. High level this aligns with our goals. A few clarifying points before we commit to the Dec 3 signature target:
- We need explicit SLA language tied to the production ramp (99.9% availability for committed capacity) 
- Procurement needs a clearly defined discount schedule by committed sustained throughput (tokens/sec) and a maximum effective discount cap
- We will want a renewal cadence baked into the MAP: how does the pilot transition to an annual committed contract and what are the re-commit triggers?

Looping in Aisha from Product and Procurement so they can weigh in on SLA and pricing mechanics. Can your team provide an example of the ramp-trigger table and the language you use for recommit milestones?

Thanks — great questions. I attached a short Ramp & Recommit example in the term sheet but below is the compact version we use operationally:

Ramp ladder (example):
- Pilot baseline: 50k tokens/day committed for 30 days (pilot price P0)
- Stage 1 ramp: >=250k tokens/day sustained for 14 days -> unlock 10% unit discount, additional reserved capacity
- Stage 2 ramp: >=1M tokens/day sustained for 30 days -> unlock further 15% discount (cumulative)
- Annual recommit trigger: sustained average >=600k tokens/day over 60 days OR explicit business KPI (X new paying users) -> option to convert to 12-month committed contract with pre-agreed uplift and renewal credits

Recommit language (proposal):
"If Customer meets the Annual Recommit Trigger within the MAP-defined measurement window, Redwood will issue a commercial conversion proposal: (i) conversion to a 12-month committed contract at pre-agreed rates, (ii) one-time onboarding/commitment credit applied at conversion, and (iii) a phased discount schedule tied to sustained throughput. If triggers are not met, parties may extend the pilot or renegotiate terms."

SLA: we can offer a 99.9% availability SLA for Dedicated pools with an escalation path and credit schedule; I’ll have legal draft the exact clause for the term sheet.

I’ll bring Marissa in to propose a recommended discount cap and uplift mechanics so Procurement has concrete numbers to review.

—Jordan

Attachments: Commercial_Term_Sheet_CW-4921.xlsx (updated: includes ramp ladder table)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procure@cloudwave.ai>, Sam Brookes <sam.brookes@cloudwave.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP & evaluation timeline — proposal for pilot -> annual commit

Thanks for looping me in — quick practical recommendations from CS/Commercial ops based on similar accounts:

1) Discount cap: recommend 25% max effective discount off list for the ladder (keeps economics predictable and preserves uplift levers at renewal).
2) Uplift credit: at conversion to annual commit, provide a one-time 10% onboarding credit applied to first invoice (not refundable).
3) Measurement windows: use rolling windows (14/30/60 days as Jordan outlined) but require a minimum observation period post-onboard (30 days) before Stage 1 discounts apply.
4) Renewal cadence: include explicit "recommit evaluation" checkpoints at 6 and 9 months with automation: if metrics exceed targets at 9 months, convert to annual with pre-approved uplift schedule; otherwise, continue on monthly committed tier or renegotiate.

Procurement — these numbers are meant to be a starting point. If you need a lower cap or fixed discount schedule we can convert to concrete line items in the term sheet.

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Hi team —

Thanks — procurement reviewed the term sheet and has two items that need addressing before we circulate a DocuSign: 
1) Cap on cumulative discounts: we want clarity on the maximum cumulative discount and whether any additional promotional credits could stack with the ramp discounts; request a firm maximum effective discount number.
2) Recommit performance gate: we require the recommit trigger to include both throughput AND a business metric (e.g., 3 production integrations or $X MRR attributable to Redwood-powered features) rather than throughput alone.

Please publish an updated term sheet with: explicit cumulative discount cap (max %), sample calculation for discount application, and the recommit gate language. Once updated, please upload to the deal link and we will circulate for signature.

Procurement (Cloudwave)

--

- Recommit gate: we’ll update the MAP to require a dual gate: (a) sustained avg >=600k tokens/day over 60 days AND (b) demonstration of business impact: >=3 customer-facing integrations or >=$250k attributable ARR within the MAP window. If both conditions are met, Redwood will present the pre-agreed conversion proposal and onboarding credit described earlier.

I updated the term sheet and uploaded both files to the deal link: https://app.redwood.com/deals/CW-2026-11-4921 — the DocuSign envelope will be created once you confirm the updated doc. Targeting the signature window still for Dec 3 for pilot commit; let me know if procurement needs more time.

Jordan
